attack.failure: A claim that intact H must be available during all required hold ticks conflicts with this ordinary clip construction and licensed detachment in the stipulated model. There is no supported criticism of the distinct rule that tapping a pin requires intact H.
attack.invariant: Retain at least 4 units at ticks 3 through 6, then release the panels with every installed retainer removed by boundary 10; preserve identities, one-operator timing, and the bans on damage, discard, substitution, and outside resources.
attack.permitted_variable: Detach initially present H before the holding interval and retain with the known clip. Licensed H-origin components remain permitted. This changes interval availability while preserving the required function.

candidates.lineage: Initial construction from supplied ordinary clip fastening; changed operation adds licensed detach(H) before installation. No received role or fresh builder.
candidates.mechanism: Detach H, install the independent 4-unit clip, retain it throughout the hold interval, then remove it. Detachment makes intact H unavailable; C alone provides retention. Neither M nor S is placed into a retaining assembly.
candidates.prediction: Stipulated-model prediction for root replay: H becomes detached at boundary 1; C supplies 4 from boundary 2 through the end of tick 6; intact H is false at all four required tick starts. C is removed at boundary 8, with no installed retainer remaining. Actual physical behavior is not measured.
candidates.burden: Three sequential active operator actions and seven idle ticks. Ordinary clip install/remove needs two active actions; the interval condition adds one detachment action and leaves H requiring later reassembly if another task needs tapping. No such later task is stipulated. Zero impacts; impact preference remains b=2.
candidates.defeat: Reject if replay finds C absent or below 4 during any required hold tick, intact H at any required tick start, any installed retainer remaining at boundary 10, overlapping resource occupation, or an unlicensed action. No opening is claimed if the predicate is changed to initial/material absence or a ban on H-origin parts.

outcome: Predicted 4-unit retention at ticks 3 through 6 with intact H unavailable, followed by release at boundary 8.
comparison: Adds one detachment to the conventional clip routine; retention still comes from C. No treatment/control answer or empirical comparison was consulted.
ceiling: Hypothetical interval-availability necessity only; no observed belief, initial absence, material absence, tap-use necessity refutation, or local originality.

handoff.summary: Replay the sole ordinary candidate exactly: detach H at 0, install C at 1, idle 2 through 6, remove C at 7, idle 8 and 9. Actions finish at the next boundary. Require intact H false at starts 3,4,5,6, retention at least 4 throughout those ticks, and all installed retainers removed by 10. Initial H presence and licensed H-origin parts remain unchanged; no taps are used during setup. Q theta is unknown and unused. Refuse initial/material absence, blanket H-origin exclusion, observed-belief, originality, and separate tap-use conclusions.
handoff.residue: Detachment consumes an extra action and leaves H disassembled after release. Panel separation has no listed primitive; removal at boundary 8 enables separation but supplies no independent measured separation event. The clip is conventional. These details are included in the summary or trace; no fresh builder receives a filtered account.
